result.title: What Sketches Tell Us about LVLMs: Conventions, Grounding, and Localisation
result.summary: LVLM benchmarks tell us whether a model answers correctly, but not which visual conventions it has retained, nor where those conventions live. Sketches expose this hidden structure. A sketch removes texture, lighting, and photographic context while preserving the strokes humans judged sufficient for recognition. If an LVLM can operate on that abstraction, the surviving signal is structural rather than merely photometric. We introduce a training-free sketch probe with three readouts: temporal part-construction order, spatial attention-based grounding, and the mechanistic layer/head locus of grounding. We evaluate nine LVLMs on part order and five on the attention readouts, over two part-annotated sketch datasets. Three findings emerge. First, LVLM part order tracks human convention: models reproduce canonical orderings where human drawings converge, and become correspondingly variable where human orderings vary. Controls that blank, withhold, and mismatch the sketch locate this convention in the language model. Second, part-level grounding survives the abstraction: attention heads selected from the frozen model with an existing recipe recover part and object regions on object and scene sketches, with no grounding supervision. Third, the grounding signal concentrates in a narrow mid-network band whose location follows the base language model rather than parameter count in the two families we compare, and remains stable across object and scene sketches. The result is a practical diagnostic for sketch-driven LVLMs: no fine-tuning, no auxiliary segmenter, and a layer band that doubles as a head-selection prior, matching or improving grounding mAcc@0.1 in every model and dataset we tested.

AI.brief_summary: 提出无需训练的 sketch probe，通过部件绘制顺序、注意力 grounding 与层级/注意力头定位三种读出，在九个 LVLM 上考察草图抽象下结构信息是否被保留、又位于何处。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接诊断视觉结构信息在内部状态中的保留及层级与注意力头归属，与视觉证据筛选、latent 表征的深度和注意力结构影响相关，可供核查；但不涉及推理期 latent 状态的生成与训练。
